messages:
linh: Heads-up: we saw intermittent TLS handshake failures from eu-ingress -> model-runtime in eu-west-1 since 02:10 UTC. Errors look like 'tlsv1 alert protocol version' in the logs.
aj: thanks — any recent RBAC or KMS changes?
rowan: I pushed a KMS policy update yesterday to tighten who can decrypt keys for ephemeral cert signing (service-account change).
maya: also rotated the intermediate used by internal CA last night (automated job). Could be related.
linh: stack traces show failed client hello for a subset of ips; both ALB and our sidecar show same.
rowan: can you paste the exact log snippet?
linh: "2026-03-19T02:14:21Z model-runtime[pid]: TLS handshake failed: tlsv1 alert protocol version from 10.4.22.9"
security-bot: :rotating_light: alert: cert-expiry-checker triggered for internal-intermediate-eu, expiry in 88 days (auto-notify).
aj: 88 days shouldn't break handshake. More likely a TLS config mismatch after the intermediate swap. Any config drift between regions?
oncall-sre: running quick probe: `openssl s_client -connect model-runtime.eu-west-1.internal:443 -tls1_2` and `-tls1_3` returns different results. Will paste.
oncall-sre: `openssl s_client -connect ... -tls1_3` -> CONNECTED, `-tls1_2` -> handshake failure.
maya: intermediate was reissued with default-min-version=tls1.3 in the signing config by mistake. I thought we kept tls1.2 allowed for older clients.
rowan: that explains it. Which services still require tls1.2? Our legacy edge proxies in ap-south-1 might.
linh: list from inventory: edge-proxy-ap-south-1, batch-ingest-eu, some infra healthchecks.

aj: Action items:
- maya: revert intermediate signing profile to allow TLS1.2 fallback until we finish clients (ETA 2h)
- rowan: update KMS key policy audit to ensure the CA signing service account still has decrypt/encrypt in all regions (ETA 1h)
- linh: identify impacted requests & sample IPs, collect pcap if possible (ETA 1h)
- oncall-sre: run cross-region handshake smoke-tests and post results here (ETA 30m)

maya: Ack. Reverting now. Command: `kubectl -n security patch configmap internal-ca --patch '{"data":{"sign_profile":"min_version: TLS1_2"}}'`
rowan: For KMS, I see one region where the role ARN was scoped to eu-west-1 only; I'll extend to eu-west-1 & eu-central-1 and document in the key policy. Will open PR.

linh: quick note on audit logging: when we change KMS policy we need to ensure CloudTrail/Stackdriver is capturing the new principal GRANTS. Otherwise we lose visibility.

aj: Good reminder — rowan, make sure the changes generate an audit-event and we forward to SIEM. Add tags `change:tls-fix` and `incident:handshake-2026-03-19`

rowan: opened PR 4823 with the policy change and added CloudTrail config check in the PR template. Link: https://git.internal/r/infra/PR/4823

security-bot: policy-change detector: detected policy diff in KMS key `internal-ca-eu`. Related PR: 4823.

oncall-sre: smoke tests after maya revert: all handshake tests now pass for tls1.2 and tls1.3 in eu-west-1 and eu-central-1. ap-south-1 still shows one failing pod (edge-proxy-02).

linh: collect pod logs from edge-proxy-02 and `tcpdump` output.

maya: I patched the signing profile, but that won't fix pods with outdated TLS client stacks. We should add a temporary routing fallback: route requests from failing clients to a legacy gateway that supports TLS1.2 only.

aj: Doable. Rowan, can infra stand up a legacy gateway in ap-south-1 for 48h window and set routing policy?

rowan: can do. I'll create a canary route and healthcheck. Also will add RBAC note: don't allow broad decrypt to the legacy gateway service account — restrict to the gateway role only.

linh: vuln triage note: we saw a CVE-2025-XXXX mention for openssl in one of the edge images. Need to confirm image versions. If we must upgrade, that could break older TLS behaviours.
maya: image is `edge-proxy:v1.3.2`. It has openssl 1.1.1k. CVE affects <1.1.1m. We'll schedule image bump but for now routing fallback is safer.

aj: After all immediate mitigations, run post-incident checklist and file a short RCA. Assign: linh (data collection), rowan (infra changes + PR), maya (signing profile rollback + rollout), aj (coordination + RCA).

oncall-sre: marking incident in incidents channel: `incident: handshake-degradation-eu-2026-03-19`

maya: quick config snippet I changed:
```
sign_profile:
  name: internal-intermediate
  min_version: TLS1_2
  allowed_ciphers: [TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256, TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256, ECDHE-ECDSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256]
```
linh: Nice. Once things are stable, let's add an automated compatibility test that runs `openssl s_client` from older client images to detect regressions on signing profile changes.

aj: agreed. Add to the CI gating for CA changes.

security-bot: Incident closed (temporary mitigations applied). Next steps: follow-up RCA and permanent testing harness.

linh: thanks everyone. Will post the collected logs and pcap summary in the incident doc within the hour. :thumbsup:
